id: Summer Meltdown-Brewtown, Upper Hutt, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
name: Summer Meltdown
venue: Brewtown, Upper Hutt, Wellington, New Zealand
long_description: A massive lineup of New Zealand music icons plays Brewtown in January. Summer Meltdown sees SIX60, Katchafire, The Black Seeds, Troy Kingi, Ria Hall and Tiki Taane take the stage on Wellington anniversary weekend. It’s set to be an unforgettable one-day music festival for all ages. Brewtown general manager Phil Gorman says, “You could build major shows around any one of these artists, so to have them all together on one bill is something we haven’t seen in Wellington before.”

id: Stan Walker — A Symphonic Experience-TSB Arena, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
name: Stan Walker — A Symphonic Experience
long_description:
With a foot in both New Zealand and Australia, Stan Walker is one of Australasia’s finest pop/R&B singers. His show, Stan Walker: A Symphonic Experience Pōneke, brings him to the capital for an evening of his biggest hits. Accompanied by his full live band and a powerful orchestra, each song has been completely reimagined to create an unforgettable night of music. From Black Box and Take It Easy to I AM, Māori Ki Te Ao, and more, this is Stan Walker elevated into something cinematic, spiritual and powerful. 

Since winning the seventh season of Australian Idol in 2009, Stan Walker has gone on to release seven albums. The concert celebrates 17 years of music-making and cultural connection. It will be a night honouring the journey and the people who have been part of it every step of the way.

id: Eric Idle — An Evening of Idle Conversation-St James Theatre, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
name: Eric Idle — An Evening of Idle Conversation
venue: St James Theatre, Wellington, New Zealand
long_description:
Relive the highs and bitter lows of one of the most beloved comedians and writers of all time. Eric Idle sits down to tell his incredible life story, live on stage at the St James Theatre in Wellington. From the giddy heights of Monty Python success to the trauma of childhood — this is unscripted and candid. The audience will also get the chance to put their own questions to him live on stage.

An Evening of Idle Conversation covers sixty years of show business. Eric will recall memories of the friends he has loved and lost including Graham Chapman, George Harrison, and Robin Williams. He’ll also cover fortunes made and squandered, feuds, reunions, a brush with cancer, and why, at 83, he is still looking on the bright side of life.

Along with five other comics Eric formed Month Python in 1969. The troupe’s absurdist sketches continue to influence comedy more fifty years later. Eric is perhaps most famous for writing the song Always Look on the Bright Side of Life, The Rutles (the world’s first mockumentary), and the musical Spamalot.

id: Blossom Valley-Aston Norwood Gardens, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
name: Blossom Valley
venue: Aston Norwood Gardens, Wellington, New Zealand
long_description:
Hosted by Aston Norwood Gardens, 350 Sakura cherry trees burst open at this springtime celebration. Visitors travel from Japan and Australia for the peak bloom. The 14-acre property offers endless photo opportunities. Daytime brings out the natural colours, while the After Dark experience illuminates the valley. Feeling peckish? There are plenty of delicious onsite refreshments. The regal Duke Restaurant & Bar hosts high tea and a refined dinner. Meanwhile, nestled in the gardens, The Stables is open at peak times to serve small bites, hot chocolate and real fruit ice cream. Don’t forget to roast a marshmallow over the fire. 

The blossoms are for everyone — families, groups, date nights, and even four-legged friends on select days. You can book a professional photoshoot to capture your time together or reserve a golf cart to explore the grounds with ease. Family passes, discounted weekday tickets, and lush onsite accommodation are all available. Book ahead to avoid disappointment. The blossom season is short and sweet.
